hints: A spanning tree connects all n cities using n-1 roads.
Sort roads by cost and accept a road only when it joins two different components.
If fewer than n-1 roads are accepted, the graph cannot be connected.
analogy: Build a network cheaply, skipping any road whose endpoints are already connected by chosen roads.
example: If edges cost 1,4,7 connect a chain, Kruskal accepts all three for total 12.
algorithm: Sort edges by weight and use disjoint-set union (DSU). Add each edge that merges two components; sum costs and check n-1 accepted edges.
correctness: Kruskal's cut/exchange property guarantees the lightest safe edge can belong to some minimum spanning tree; DSU prevents cycles and connectivity requires n-1 edges.
complexity: O(m log m) time and O(n) DSU space.
